∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ) (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m) (h_H001 : 1 ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ m) (h_H002 : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u (domain n)) (h_H003 : ‖q‖ = 1) (h_H004 : ∀ x : X n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ‖u (x,t)‖ = 1) (h_H005 : ∀ x : X n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, dt (dt u) (x,t) - lap u (x,t) = a • u (x,t)) (h_H006 : ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (X n), IsCompact C ∧ ∀ x : X n, x ∉ C → ∀ r : ℝ, r ∈ Icc s t → u (x,r) = q), (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t →
  Integrable (fun x : X n => density u (x,t)) (mu n) ∧
  DifferentiableAt ℝ (energy u) t ∧ deriv (energy u) t = 0) ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → energy u s = energy u t)

correspondence.explanation: The full theorem quantifies arbitrary positive dimensions n,m, a jointly smooth map and a single fixed unit vector q with exactly H001–H006. Natural dimension indices subject to H001 are precisely the original positive integer dimensions. The standard coordinates X n with product Lebesgue measure and Euclidean V m identify the original spaces and integrals; Fin n enumerates each original spatial coordinate once. Replacing a map on positive times by an arbitrary real-time extension is reversible by restriction: the positive-time domain is open, so smoothness and every derivative in H005 and the conclusion depend only on the restriction; any source map may be extended arbitrarily outside it. H004 is the original sphere constraint, H005 is pointwise existence of a real normal multiplier with no regularity imposed, and H006 is the same compact perturbation from the fixed q uniformly on each positive closed time interval. The conclusion asserts absolute spatial integrability for every positive time, actual differentiability and derivative zero of the integral of density, and equality of that energy at every pair of positive times. Its norm squares and finite coordinate sum have exactly coefficient one; integrability makes the Bochner scalar integral the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. No assertion or smooth extension condition is imposed at time zero.
